collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — ADVICE AND DECISIONS (ADV-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Asking for advice, giving it, ignoring it, following half of it, and deciding alone. Advice can be wrong, even from elders and experts. Following it doesn't guarantee a good outcome and ignoring it doesn't cause a bad one. Feeling heard with no decision is a perfectly good ending, and nobody ever has to admit someone else was right.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: A villager asks a friend's honest opinion of a carving that may be a bird or a fish: the friend is honest, or kind.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) has carved a figure for the doorpost of (subject.his/her) hut. It's a bird. Or possibly a fish. (subject.He/she) holds it up to (friend). "Be honest. What do you think?" (friend) looks at it for a long time.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: "Honestly?" says (friend). "I'm not sure what it is. But I like the wings. Or fins." (subject) laughs. "It's a bird." "Then the wings are great and the face could be more birdy." (subject) thinks about it. Then (subject.he/she) puts it up on the doorpost exactly as it is. "I like it fishy," (subject.he/she) decides. It's (subject.his/her) door.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: "I love it," says (friend). (subject) narrows (subject.his/her) eyes. "You said honest." "I am being honest," says (friend). "I love that you made it. I have no idea what it is." (subject) laughs so hard (subject.he/she) nearly drops it. It goes on the doorpost. Visitors guess something different every time. (subject) never tells.
